scenes.title: CASE STUDY No.002 — RESIDENTIAL INTRUSION MITIGATION SYSTEM

sentences.text: This film examines a residential intrusion mitigation system at a seasonal family property.
The system operated with one on-site manager and no new equipment budget.
The facility was a large suburban residence.
One eight-year-old manager remained on site during scheduled family travel.
Two unauthorized visitors later tested the property.
Senior management remained temporarily international.
On-site management attendance was therefore one hundred percent.
Visual occupancy simulation used cardboard personnel, a model train, music, and lighting.
The simulated guests moved continuously, so the residence appeared active from the street.
The system required no additional payroll.
Performance under close inspection was outside the approved test range.
The facility used several independent layers of intrusion mitigation.
Exterior ice reduced safe access to the property.
Door hardware provided a strong thermal warning.
Glass decorations controlled walking routes inside the facility.
Two gravity-assisted paint containers protected the main staircase.
A recorded communications officer handled external conversations.
A portable biological unit provided additional distraction.
The residence maintained site control during every test.
The two unauthorized visitors experienced repeated safety incidents.
A local response partner completed the final intervention.
Intrusion mitigation was rated excellent.
Unauthorized visitor satisfaction was rated low.
Resident comfort remained mixed.
Continued habitability was approved with minor redesign.
Light, sound, and visible movement should operate together.
Visual occupancy simulation works best beyond the recommended inspection distance.
A single security control may be bypassed.
Layered systems perform better because each system supports the others.
Gravity remains a cost-effective security subcontractor.
Gravity-assisted equipment requires sufficient ceiling clearance.
Local response partners can reduce emergency response delay.
A nearby partner may complete tasks that automated systems cannot finish.

scenes.title: END OF LESSON

Please return all biological units and paint containers to approved storage areas.
